q: Lusin's theorem in measure theory states that for a measurable function f on a finite measure space:
opts: f equals a continuous function a.e.
For any ε > 0, there exists a closed set F with μ(Fᶜ) < ε on which f is continuous
f has at most countably many discontinuities
exp: Lusin's theorem: measurable functions are 'nearly continuous'—continuous when restricted to a large closed set. This justifies approximating measurable by continuous functions.
